item.title: LLMKube: Arbitrary Host File Read via Model.spec.source hostPath Injection
item.description:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 7.7 (v3.1)
Summary: ### Summary LLMKube's `ModelReconciler` accepts arbitrary absolute paths and `file://` URIs in the `Model.spec.source` field and propagates them to two distinct sinks without path allowlisting: (1) `os.Open()` inside the controller pod itself (`copyLocalModel`), and (2) a Kubernetes `HostPathVolumeSource` that mounts the attacker-supplied path into the inference pod's init container. Any namespace user with permission to create or update `Model` and `InferenceService` custom resources can read arbitrary files accessible to the controller pod (e.g., the controller's own Kubernetes service-account token) or arbitrary files on the node where the inference pod is scheduled (e.g., `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf`). Model caching, the feature that activates the `hostPath` sink, is **enabled by default** in both the CLI and the official Helm chart. CVSS v3.1 Base Score: **7.7 (High)**. ### Detail

item.description:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 7.5 (v3.1)
Summary: ## Description `bin/install-from-cache.js` downloads a prebuilt native addon (`*.node`) over the network and writes it directly to the artifact path **with no cryptographic integrity verification of any kind** - no checksum manifest, no signature, no SRI. item.title: Forge: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature forgery via non-canonical DigestInfo encoding
item.description:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 7.5 (v3.1)
Summary: ### Summary RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 signature verification (`publicKey.verify()` with the default scheme, also used by X.509 certificate and PKCS#7 verification) accepted non-canonical BER encodings of the DigestInfo, such as NULL parameters with content and non-minimal lengths. These leave attacker-controlled bytes inside an accepted DigestInfo, which allows signatures to be forged without the private key for RSA keys with a low public exponent (e=3). item.title: code-review-mcp-server: Command injection via unsanitized folderPath/baseBranch parameters
item.description:
Severity: HIGH
Summary: ### Impact `code-review-mcp-server` exposes MCP tools (`getLocalGitDiff`, `codeReview`, `createPR`, `getPRTemplate`) that accept `folderPath` and `baseBranch` string parameters. These caller-controlled values were interpolated directly into shell command strings executed via `child_process.execSync()`, which runs commands through `/bin/sh`. A crafted value such as `baseBranch = "main; <arbitrary command> #"` (or a `$(...)` command substitution, or a `folderPath` that breaks out of the surrounding quotes) results in **arbitrary command execution** on the host running the MCP server. ### Patches Fixed in **1.5.3**. Every `execSync()` call was replaced with `execFileSync()` using argument arrays, so inputs are passed directly to `git` / `gh` without going through a shell, eliminating the injection at its root. ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to `code-review-mcp-server@1.5.3` or later.
Suggested next step: Check whether affected package versions are present in your dependencies and review the maintainer's fix guidance.
Original advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jq3q-62jc-fqq9
Watchlist match only. Local exposure has not been assessed.

item.title: NLTK dot2img runs Graphviz 'dot' without the trusted-exec chokepoint, enabling local code execution via a writable PATH element
item.description:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 7.8 (v3.1)
Summary: ## Summary `nltk.parse.dependencygraph.dot2img` invokes the Graphviz `dot` executable without the trusted-execution guarantees that NLTK applies to its other native-tool wrappers. The function resolves `dot` by bare name and then runs the resolved absolute path with a raw `subprocess.run`, omitting the ownership/writability check and the loader-environment scrub that `nltk.pathsec.spawn_trusted` provides. The advisory GHSA-6hwm-xvph-95vm (CVE-2026-78680) addressed the same untrusted-search-path class for the Graphviz `dot` invoker in `nltk/tran
Suggested next step: Check whether affected package versions are present in your dependencies and review the maintainer's fix guidance.
